grades.quote: The operating system removes the file when it no longer has any names and is no longer in use by any process. (An open file can continue to exist without any names, as you can demonstrate in Exploration Project 8.10.)
grades.reason: The passage explains that unlink removes only a name, not the file. The file is deleted only when it has no names and no process is using it, so an open file can persist without names. It also notes that a file can have multiple names. This directly explains why a file can still be read after unlink.
